journey.title: Open the filters drawer and apply a filter with the keyboard
journey.goal: Opening the drawer moves focus into it, so the user can tick a filter and show results without a pointer

functionalJourney.title: Apply a filter with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking Filters, ticking Waterproof and clicking Show results applies the filter

guards.title: Escape closes the drawer and returns focus to Filters
guards.goal: After opening the drawer with the pointer, Escape closes it and focus is back on the Filters button

plan.root_cause: The drawer does not move focus to its content when opened, leaving focus on the triggering button or body, preventing keyboard users from interacting with filters.
plan.repair_strategy: Override the show method in the Drawer class to focus the first focusable element (respecting autofocus) after the dialog is shown.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Focus will be moved into the drawer when opened, allowing keyboard users to tab to the close button, checkboxes, and apply button without needing a pointer.
functional_risks: If the drawer already defines an autofocus attribute, our logic will respect it by selecting that element first.
If no focusable elements exist inside the drawer, focus will be set on the drawer itself, which is harmless.
Potential minor overhead from the selector lookup, but negligible.
verification_requirements: After opening the drawer with Enter, focus should be on the first focusable element (e.g., #filters-close).
Subsequent Tab presses should move focus to the In stock checkbox, then Waterproof checkbox, then Apply button.
Escape key should close the drawer and return focus to the Filters toggle button.
Mouse interactions should continue to work as before.
The drawer should still be closable via the close button and backdrop click.

attempts.failure: Candidate build failed: [{"file":"js/src/drawer.ts","pass":false,"kind":"syntax","message":"TypeScript is not erasable or its JavaScript has a syntax error"}]

plan.root_cause: The drawer.ts file has two issues causing TypeScript build failure: (1) missing import for the Data module used in _hideChildComponents, and (2) arrow functions in _initSwipe returning Promise<void> from hide() where SwipeConfig expects () => void, creating a type mismatch that the build system reports as a syntax error.
plan.repair_strategy: Add the missing Data import from './dom/data.js' and wrap each this.hide() call in a block statement () => { this.hide() } so the callback returns void, matching SwipeConfig callback signatures.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Fixes the TypeScript build error so that subsequent accessibility fixes (e.g., focus management in drawer) can be compiled and verified.
functional_risks: Swipe dismiss callbacks will call hide() but not await the returned promise; this matches the Swipe.execute behavior which does not await callbacks.
Adding the Data import has no runtime side effects; it only makes the existing _hideChildComponents code type-check correctly.

Drawer swipe-to-dismiss functionality still works (manual test).

plan.root_cause: The Drawer component does not move focus into the dialog when opened, leaving focus on the trigger button. Additionally, the drawer.ts file has TypeScript build errors: missing Data import and swipe callback type mismatches (arrow functions returning Promise<void> where () => void is expected).
plan.repair_strategy: Apply three minimal fixes to drawer.ts: (1) add missing Data import, (2) wrap each this.hide() call in _initSwipe with block statements to match SwipeConfig callback signatures, (3) override show() to focus the first focusable element (respecting autofocus) after the dialog opens.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: When the drawer opens via keyboard (Enter on trigger), focus moves to the first focusable element inside (e.g., close button), allowing immediate Tab navigation to checkboxes and Apply button without a pointer.
functional_risks: If the drawer already has an autofocus attribute, that element receives focus first (correct behavior).
If no focusable elements exist, focus lands on the dialog element itself (harmless).
Swipe dismiss callbacks now return void, matching SwipeConfig; hide() promise is not awaited (matches existing Swipe.execute behavior).
Adding Data import has no runtime side effects; only satisfies type-checking for _hideChildComponents.
verification_requirements: TypeScript compilation passes with no syntax or type errors in drawer.ts.
Opening the drawer with Enter moves focus to #filters-close (or first focusable).
Subsequent Tab presses move focus to #in-stock, #waterproof, #apply in order.
Escape key closes drawer and returns focus to #filters-open.
Mouse interactions (click trigger, click close, click backdrop) continue to work.
